hypothesis: Adding an outer non-structural skip loop to LineIndex.build (outside strings, once lineHasContent is true, advance i over every byte whose Uint8Array(256) class entry is 0, i.e. anything except '"' '{' '[' '}' ']' '\n', before the switch) removes per-byte switch dispatch for the ~25% of bytes that sit outside strings, with identical output. Single change: only the outside-string path of the existing for-loop gains the skip; the string branch, checkpoint logic, record pushes, for-await loop and all state locals are unchanged.

steps.change: In build, line 246, change `const b = buf[i];` to `let b = buf[i];`. Leave the `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` header (L245) and the inString block (L247-251: escaped / 0x5c / 0x22 handling and `continue`) byte-for-byte unchanged.

Semantics review (no code change; executor must confirm each before benchmarking): (a) lineHasContent: skip only runs when it is already true, so whitespace-only and empty lines still go byte-by-byte through the default branch, and the first non-whitespace byte still sets it; '\n' is in OCLS so it is never skipped and still resets lineHasContent=false. (b) CRLF: 0x0d is skipped only when lineHasContent is true (default branch would ignore it anyway); on a content-free line it still reaches default and is ignored; the following 0x0a is structural. (c) Depth clamp: '}' and ']' are in OCLS, so `if (depth > 0) depth--` runs for every closer. (d) Strings: '"' is in OCLS so string entry always goes through case 0x22; a backslash outside a string is non-structural (default branch only sets lineHasContent) and may be skipped. (e) Chunk-boundary resume: `break` exits only the per-chunk for-loop when the skip hits n; inString/escaped/depth/lineHasContent/line/startOff are untouched by skipped bytes, and the next chunk restarts at i=0. (f) Dangling EOF structures: EOF block reads the same depth/inString/lineHasContent/startOff values as before, so dangling-object, dangling-string and trailing-newline-after-dangling cases are unchanged. (g) Non-ASCII bytes (>=0x80) and string chunks via Buffer.from are skipped/handled identically to the default branch.

Verify: run the project's typecheck/build and test scripts from package.json (must pass with zero new errors), then run `node scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` at least 3 times and report the primary score (speedup vs reference) and the correctness sub-score for each run. Correctness must be 1. Do not edit the benchmark or any file other than src/indexer/lineIndex.ts.

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: ~0% standalone (expected score ~0.88-0.94 vs baseline 0.898, within the ±0.05-0.08 noise band). Value is as a stack partner: research measured +10-20% when combined with an unrolled/SWAR string loop (rej8 1.25 -> 1.50; swar 1.35 -> 1.54/1.68).
expected_outcome.rationale: 75% of fixture bytes are inside strings and this plan deliberately leaves the string branch untouched, so at most ~25% of bytes can benefit, and many outside-string bytes are already structural or on content-free prefixes. Scratch measurement of this exact change on the current per-byte string code was 0.916 and 0.903 (neutral vs mirror 0.79-0.91). It is submitted honestly as a neutral-alone architecture change so H003 is satisfied this round and so it can be stacked on the optimization-family string loop in round 3, where the outer switch becomes a larger share of the remaining cost.
